rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed 3.75–4.00%, Dec hike ~83% (from ~78% a.m.); ECB held 2.50% Oct 29, Dec 17 hike >80%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%, Dec ~85%; RBA Nov 3 hike ~79–85%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%; BoC 2.50%, Dec ~45%; RBNZ 2.75%
rows.read: Most central banks still lean toward higher rates because of energy-driven inflation. Strong US figures kept a December Fed hike likely, and the European Central Bank's chief said a hike was discussed, which pointed to December. Japan's central bank decides overnight and is expected to wait.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US Q3 GDP 3.4% ann. (fc 3.2%); claims 194K; euro-area sentiment 96.9 (fc 97.5); UK mortgage approvals 53.4K (fc 54K); Italy unemployment 6.3%
rows.read: The US economy is growing far faster than Europe's, and that gap keeps favouring the dollar. Euro-area sentiment slipped again and UK borrowing cooled, while US jobless claims stayed very low.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US PCE 3.6% y/y (from 3.4%); core +0.3% m/m, 3.1% y/y (in line); Tokyo core CPI tonight fc 2.6%; euro-area flash CPI Fri (prior 3.8%)
rows.read: Energy keeps prices high, which is why most central banks still lean toward hikes. US inflation rose on gasoline, but underlying prices did only what was expected, so there was no fresh shock. Euro-area and Tokyo price figures come next.

rows.title: Risk
rows.figure: USD/JPY ~157.97; USD/CHF ~0.8262; Vance letter to Iran (WSJ); Hormuz ship fire, cause under investigation (UKMTO)
rows.read: Markets stayed calm, with no rush into safe currencies like the yen and franc. Hopes for US–Iran talks eased war fears a little, while a ship fire near the Strait of Hormuz was a reminder the risk has not gone.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$113.82 (-1.3%), WTI ~$101.09 (-1.6%, midday CT); US gas storage +80 Bcf; OPEC+ meets Sunday
rows.read: Oil fell again on hopes the US and Iran might talk, but it is still far above pre-war levels. That keeps helping exporters like Canada and Australia and costing importers like Japan and the euro area. A real peace deal would shift that balance quickly.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD and EUR (euro net short largest since March 2020), for GBP and AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and the loonie's climb since Canada's rate hike puts those bets under pressure. Their bets against the euro are the largest in years, so good euro news could force them to buy it back.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Lagarde: tools to counter disorderly French bond moves; French revenue vote Nov 3; Italy 10-y auction 4.49% (from 4.58%); UK headroom £15bn
rows.read: France's budget fight is still unresolved and keeps a weight on the euro, though the European Central Bank's chief said the bank has tools to calm any disorderly bond selling. The UK Budget passed calmly, so British bonds and the pound took it in stride.
